Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (*al-Kashshaf*, "The Unveiler") on Surah 28, verse 82:

It may be said "yesterday" (al-ams) without meaning the day before your day. Rather, the recent time is used figuratively, *makānahu* meaning its rank in the world. *Wa* ("alas") is separated from *ka-anna* ("as if"), and it is a word that signals an error and expresses regret. Its meaning is:

The people became aware of their error in their wish and their saying, ﴿Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given﴾, and they regretted it. Then they said, ﴿And it is as if the disbelievers do not prosper﴾. That is, "How similar the situation is to the fact that the disbelievers do not attain success." This is the view of al-Khalil (ibn Ahmad) and Sibawayh. He said:

*Wa, kaʾanna man yakun lahu nashab yuhabbab...
wa man yaftaqir yaʾish ʿaysha darr*

*[[sa'altanī al-ṭalāq an ra'atā...
qul māli qad jiʾtumānī bi-nukr]]*

*Alas, as if the one who has wealth is loved,
and the one who is poor lives a life of hardship.
He is avoided in secret talk, but
the owner of wealth is present at every secret.*

This is by Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl al-Qurashi. It is also said to be by Saʿid ibn Zayd, one of the ten who were given glad tidings of Paradise. It is also said to be by Nubayh ibn al-Hajjaj ibn ʿAmir, who was killed as a disbeliever on the day of Badr.

*Sa'altanī* with the *hamza* changed to *alif* for the metre, which is a rare dialect form. The pronoun refers to his two wives. *Al-ṭalāq* is the second object. *An ra'atā* means "because of their seeing". *Qul* may be a past verb, in which case it requires a deleted element before it to complete the sense, meaning: "Because they saw me (that) my wealth is little", or "because of their seeing that I am (now) poor". Or it may be a noun meaning "little", with no deletion, so the meaning is: "Because they saw that my wealth is little", i.e., my little wealth. The address shifts from the third person to the second person with the words *qad jiʾtumānī bi-nukr*, meaning "you have come to me with what is abominable (munkar)". This carries a sense of amazement at their condition. *Wa* is a verb-noun (*ism fiʿl*) expressing wonder. It is also said that its form signals alertness and regret. *Ka-anna* is used either for supposition or for certainty, as the Kufans permitted. It is the lightened form of the heavy *inna*, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter. It is also said that the lightened form has no noun.

*Al-nashab* means wealth. *Yaʿish ʿaysha darr* means "he hates". *Al-najiyy*, with the doubled letter, means the one who speaks in secret, i.e., the one who speaks privately.

*Yujannab* is in the passive form. *Sirr* is its second object. *Akhā al-māl* means the owner of wealth. *Muḥḍar* is a passive participle, and *kull* is its second object.

Al-Farraʾ related that a Bedouin woman said to her husband, "Where is your son?" He said, "Wa, as if he were behind the tent." According to the Kufans, *wayka* means *waylaka* ("woe to you"), and the meaning is: "Do you not know that the disbelievers do not prosper?" It is also permissible that the *kaf* is the particle of address joined to *wa*, as in the line:

*...... wayka ʿantar aqdim
[[wa-laqad shafā nafsī wa-adhhaba suqmahā...
qīl al-fawāris wayka ʿantar aqdim]]*

*...And truly he healed my soul and took away its sickness,
(when) the knights said, "Woe to you, ʿAntar, advance!"*

This is by ʿAntarah ibn Shaddad from his *Muʿallaqa*. Another reading is *wa-abarr asqamahā* ("and he cured its sicknesses"). Another reading is *wa-adhhaba ghammahā* ("and he removed its grief"). Another reading has *qawl* instead of *qīl*. Both are verbal nouns. *Wayka* is a verb-noun expressing wonder, but it does not fit the line well. It is also said to be a word of alertness, with the *kaf* as a particle of address. Al-Kisaʾi said the origin of *wayka* is *waylaka*, so the *kaf* is a pronoun in the genitive case, but its fit with the line is weak. *ʿAntar* is a vocative with truncation (*tarkhīm*). Truncation and dropping the vocative particle are good here because the situation calls for urgency and quick speech. *Aqdim* means "advance against the enemy, so that he may protect us from its might."

And *anna* means *li-anna* ("because"). The *lam* is to explain the reason for the statement. Or the meaning is: "Because the disbelievers do not prosper, that happened," namely the sinking of Qarun into the earth. Some people pause at *wa* and begin with *ka-anna*, and some pause at *wayka*.

Al-Aʿmash read *law-lā mann Allāh ʿalaynā* ("if not for God's favour upon us"). It was also read *la-khasafa bi-nā* ("it would have sunk us into the earth"). Here the statement "it was read *la-khasafa bi-nā*" indicates that the well-known reading is *la-khasafa*, in the passive form. (ʿ)

In it is the pronoun of God.

*Wa-lā nakhsif bi-nā*, like your saying, *inqaṭaʿa bihi* ("he was cut off"). And *la-takhsif bi-nā* ("it would sink us into the earth").

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 28, verse 83:

﴿That﴾ is an exaltation of it and a magnification of its status. That is, the one you have heard of and whose description has reached you. The promise [[His phrase "lam yu'alliq al-mawʿid" is perhaps "al-waʿd". (ʿ)]] was not made conditional on abandoning haughtiness and corruption, but on abandoning the desire for them and the inclination of the hearts toward them, as He said: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have wronged, lest the Fire touch you﴾. So He attached the threat to inclining (ruknah). It is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man may be pleased that the thong of his sandal is finer than the thong of his companion's sandal, and so he enters under this verse. It is also related from al-Fudayl that he recited it and then said: [[Mahmud said: "The promise is not made conditional on abandoning haughtiness and corruption, but on abandoning the desire for them, as the Exalted said: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have wronged, for the Fire will touch you﴾, so He attached the threat to inclining toward the wrongdoers. It is related from ʿAli that a man may be pleased that the thong of his sandal is better than the thong of his brother's sandal, and so he enters under this verse. It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz that he kept repeating it until he died. It is related from al-Fudayl that he recited it and said: 'Here the wishes have gone.' Among the covetous are those who attribute haughtiness to Pharaoh and corruption to Qarun, citing His words ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾ and His words ﴿And seek not corruption in the land﴾, and they say: whoever is not like Pharaoh and Qarun, for him is that Final Abode. They do not reflect on His words ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ as ʿAli, ʿUmar and al-Fudayl reflected on it." Ahmad said: This is a disparagement of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah), for every monotheist is among the people of Paradise. They hoped only where Allah had given them hope, and indeed He confirmed their hope in His mercy when His Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, 'There is no god but Allah,' enters Paradise, even if he commits adultery and even if he steals," three times, and in the third time: "even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in the dust." O Allah, grant us from the hope of Your mercy that which protects us from despair, and from Your fear that which comes between us and Your disobedience. And Allah is the Granter of success to what is right.]]. It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz that he kept repeating it until he died. Among the covetous are those who attribute haughtiness to Pharaoh and corruption to Qarun, relying on His words ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾ and ﴿And seek not corruption in the land﴾, and they say: whoever is not like Pharaoh and Qarun, for him is that Final Abode. They do not reflect on His words ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ as ʿAli, al-Fudayl and ʿUmar reflected on it.

It means: "they will not be recompensed," so the phrase "those who did the evil deeds" is placed in the position of the pronoun, because attributing the doing of evil deeds to them is repeated. This carries a stronger censure of their condition and an added loathing of evil deeds in the hearts of the listeners. "Except what they used to do" means only the like of what they used to do. This is from His great bounty and wide generosity: that evil is not repaid except with its like, while good is repaid with ten times its like, and with seven hundred, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 28, verse 85:

﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an﴾ means: He who obligated you to recite it, convey it, and act upon what is in it. The meaning is that the One who has made you bear the hardship of this duty will reward you for it with a reward that no description can encompass. ﴿And will surely return you to a place of return﴾ means: to a return (ma'ad) that belongs to no one other than you among mankind. The indefiniteness of "ma'ad" is for this reason. It has also been said that what is meant is Makkah. Its basis is that the meaning is that He would return him to it on the Day of the Conquest. The reason for indefiniteness is that on that day it was a return of great stature and a place of pride, because of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) dominance over it, his subduing of its people, and the manifestation of the might of Islam and its people and the humiliation of polytheism and its party. The surah is Meccan, so it is as if Allah promised him, while he was in Makkah suffering harm and subjugation from its people, that He would make him emigrate from it and return him to it, outwardly victorious and triumphant. It has also been said that it was revealed to him when he reached al-Juhfah on his migration, and he longed for his birthplace, the birthplace of his forefathers, and the sanctuary of Ibrahim. Then Jibril descended and said to him: "Do you long for Makkah?" He said: "Yes," so he revealed it to him.

If you say: how is the statement of the Exalted, ﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance﴾, connected to what precedes it? I say: when He promised His Messenger a return to a place of return, He said: say to the polytheists, ﴿My Lord knows best who has come with guidance﴾, meaning himself and what he deserves of reward in his return, ﴿and who is in clear error﴾, meaning them and what they deserve of punishment in their return.

"If you should say: What is the construction of the exception in His words, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾? I say: This is a statement that is to be understood according to its sense, as if it had been said: "And the Book was not cast down to you except as a mercy from your Lord." And it is permissible that ﴿illa﴾ (except) here carries the meaning of ﴿lākin﴾ (but), for the purpose of correction (istidrak), meaning: "But it was cast down to you as a mercy from your Lord."

Recited also: "yasuddanka" (yaṣuddanaka), from aṣadda, which has the same meaning as ṣaddahu (to turn away, to block), and this is the dialect of Kalb. He said:

"People who turned others away from them with the sword,
turning away like the water-wheels turned from the nostrils of the thirsty camels."

[The explanation of this line was given earlier in the second part, page 538; refer to it if you wish. Its corrector.]

*Ba'da idh unzilat ilayka* (after it was sent down to you): after the time of its being sent down. *Idh* is attached to time-words, as when you say: *hinaidhin* (at that time), *laylataidhin* (on that night), *yawmaidhin* (on that day), and what is similar to that. The prohibition against supporting the disbelievers and the like is of the kind of stirring-up (tahyij) whose mention has been preceded.

The Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 28, verse 88:

﴿Everything perishes except His Face﴾ (except Him). "The Face" is used to express the Essence (dhat).

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ta-Sin-Mim al-Qasas (Surah 28), he will have a reward equal to the number of those who affirmed Musa and those who denied him. And no angel will remain in the heavens and the earth without bearing witness for him on the Day of Resurrection that he was truthful, [that] everything perishes except His Face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned."

[Narrated by al-Tha'labi and Ibn Mardawayh. And al-Wahidi from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with their chains of narration mentioned earlier.]
